newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates dip as liquidity is ample.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates dip as liquidity is ample.

text.p: Sufficient market liquidity helped German call money rates ease to 3.00/3.05 percent on Thursday from Wednesday's 3.02/3.05 percent rates.
"Nobody paid 3.05 percent anymore today," said one dealer.
Despite more ample liquidity conditions, traders still ruled out a further drop in rates as governments likely will need more funds ahead of the monthly tax payment date.

The market does not expect the Bundesbank council to adjust any of its three key interest rates at today's council meeting, dealers said, adding the central bank will likely set its next repos at a fixed three percent rate.
Economists said that there were very few good reasons for the Bundesbank to lower its 2.50 percent discount and 4.50 percent Lombard rates at the moment.
Dealers said the Bundesbank may soon announce changes in its reserve requirement policies, but said they were not sure whether the announcement could come as soon as today.
German banks have long lobbied the central bank to ease its reserve requiremenst for repo business in order to pull back some of the business currently conducted abroad.
Dealers look for call money rates to trade sideways for the remainder of the week, barring unforseen Bundesbank decisions.

Banks held 39.1 billion marks at the Bundesbank on Wednesday, down from 41.3 billion marks held one day earlier and the average monthly holdings stood at 41.0 billion marks, down from 41.4 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.05133 percent on Thursday compared with 3.06200 percent on Wednesday.
